./docs/dev-log/scout/2026-10-01-auto-fa-rank-design/engine-contract.md:13:For a common `T=4` cell, generic covariance dimensions after rotational redundancy are `q_G(K)=TK-K(K-1)/2+T`: K=0 diagonal has 4; K=1 FA has 8; K=2 has 11. The current FA optimizer coordinates for K=1 are 4 loading values plus 4 uniqueness values; residual `R0` contributes `T(T+1)/2=10` parameters in both candidates. Thus the floor-matched K=0 selector candidate has 14 covariance parameters and K=1 has 18 under this generic count; the fixed intercept coefficients are common to both models, with four fixed coefficients for an intercept-only four-trait design [src/multivariate.jl:660-671, 693-723, 1041-1055]. The T=4 K=2 count exceeds the ambient 10-dimensional genetic covariance and is excluded in the current plan; the count screen is not an identification proof [docs/design/auto-fa-rank-design-plan-20261001.md, Symbolic alignment required first].
./docs/dev-log/scout/2026-10-01-auto-fa-rank-design/engine-contract.md:17:There is no `method=:ML` argument in this fitter: it optimizes the full-constant Gaussian REML objective only. Its log-likelihood includes `(N-p')log(2π)`, and the implementation explicitly says comparisons require matched data and compatible fixed-effect spaces [src/multivariate.jl:844-856, 917-934, 1010-1021]. Both genetic structures append the same `T(T+1)/2` log-Cholesky residual covariance coordinates and use the same `_mv_reml_loglik_core`, so they can be evaluated under the same REML objective at identical `Y, X, Z, Ainv`; nesting still requires the selector-only floor-matched diagonal parameterization above. This does not settle whether REML information criteria are defensible for rank choice, what sample-size convention BIC should use for multivariate repeated records, or whether an ML objective should be added for selection. Those are open C0 method decisions in the design plan, not current engine capabilities [docs/design/auto-fa-rank-design-plan-20261001.md, ticket C0].
./docs/dev-log/scout/2026-10-01-auto-fa-rank-design/engine-contract.md:25:FA diagnostics expose strategy, attempted starts, selected start, objective range, relative G/R disagreement, a better valid nonconverged-start flag, minimum uniqueness, distance to the absolute `1e-4` uniqueness floor, near-floor flag, and per-start loglik/valid/converged/iterations/floor details [src/multivariate.jl:409-417, 1137-1167]. These are optimizer-start diagnostics for one fitted rank. They do not provide a cross-rank attempt table, an eligibility rule for rank selection, retry budget, criterion differences, a boundary/no-signal flag for the diagonal candidate, or rank-selection uncertainty. Convergence and positive Ledermann slack are not identification checks [src/multivariate.jl:419-460; docs/design/auto-fa-rank-design-plan-20261001.md, Required acceptance content].

docs/dev-log/scout/2026-10-01-auto-fa-rank-design/engine-contract.md:13:For a common `T=4` cell, generic covariance dimensions after rotational redundancy are `q_G(K)=TK-K(K-1)/2+T`: K=0 diagonal has 4; K=1 FA has 8; K=2 has 11. The current FA optimizer coordinates for K=1 are 4 loading values plus 4 uniqueness values; residual `R0` contributes `T(T+1)/2=10` parameters in both candidates. Thus the floor-matched K=0 selector candidate has 14 covariance parameters and K=1 has 18 under this generic count; the fixed intercept coefficients are common to both models, with four fixed coefficients for an intercept-only four-trait design [src/multivariate.jl:660-671, 693-723, 1041-1055]. The T=4 K=2 count exceeds the ambient 10-dimensional genetic covariance and is excluded in the current plan; the count screen is not an identification proof [docs/design/auto-fa-rank-design-plan-20261001.md, Symbolic alignment required first].
docs/dev-log/scout/2026-10-01-auto-fa-rank-design/engine-contract.md:17:There is no `method=:ML` argument in this fitter: it optimizes the full-constant Gaussian REML objective only. Its log-likelihood includes `(N-p')log(2π)`, and the implementation explicitly says comparisons require matched data and compatible fixed-effect spaces [src/multivariate.jl:844-856, 917-934, 1010-1021]. Both genetic structures append the same `T(T+1)/2` log-Cholesky residual covariance coordinates and use the same `_mv_reml_loglik_core`, so they can be evaluated under the same REML objective at identical `Y, X, Z, Ainv`; nesting still requires the selector-only floor-matched diagonal parameterization above. This does not settle whether REML information criteria are defensible for rank choice, what sample-size convention BIC should use for multivariate repeated records, or whether an ML objective should be added for selection. Those are open C0 method decisions in the design plan, not current engine capabilities [docs/design/auto-fa-rank-design-plan-20261001.md, ticket C0].
